post.text:
🚨 THE TIP SCREEN IS LYING - AND IT KNOWS YOU WON’T CHECK

"They're trying to trick us.”

A woman records the checkout screen after her bill comes out to $60.50.

She taps 18%.
The screen claims the tip is almost $30.

She stops and does the math herself.

“That’s not 18%,” she https://t.co/c3siYD88ge

description.description: A close-up of a Ziosk payment tablet at a restaurant table. The tablet displays a check amount of $60.50. A finger interacts with the screen, selecting different tip percentages. When 18% is selected, the calculated tip displays as $29.88 (incorrectly calculated), and when 20% is selected, the tip displays as $33.20 (also incorrectly calculated).

tweetMedia.transcription: Don't just punch in 15 or 18% because my check came out to 60 and they're saying 18% is almost $30 out of 60. That's a 50% tip. So they're trying to trick us. Look if you hit 20 it makes it 33. 18, 29. That's not right. So it's actually $12. I think 20% is actually $12. Don't get bamboozled. Don't just start clicking stuff.
